summary: Khao soi from Chiang Mai, a recipe from the Herbivoracious cookbook: fresh egg noodles in a spicy coconut-milk broth built on a homemade dried chile curry paste, topped with fried tofu, crispy fried noodles, pickled mustard greens or cabbage and lime; 1 hour total.
glance: Prep 20 min, cook 40 min, total 1 hr
3/4 to 1 1/2 pounds packaged fried tofu, depending on the type
crispy noodles, pickled mustard greens or napa cabbage, lime

summary: Celery and fennel salad, a riff on one at Bastille in Seattle: thinly sliced celery and fennel in olive oil, lemon and Maldon salt, with slowly fried pumpernickel croutons and paper-thin shavings of frozen blue cheese; prep 15 minutes, cook 10.
glance: pumpernickel fried in 260°F oil about 10 minutes
compress the celery and fennel in a chamber vacuum, or freeze and thaw them the day before
faq: What is the origin of this salad?

A riff on a celery salad at Bastille in Seattle, served as a vegetarian course at a "whole beast feast." Theirs had tiny pumpernickel croutons and baby artichokes; this one uses fennel instead, with shaved frozen blue cheese for a garnish.
Why use frozen blue cheese?
A trick the author learned from Grant Crilly: freeze a small block of blue cheese hard and shave paper-thin slices over each salad with a mandoline or vegetable peeler immediately before serving.
Do I need a chamber vacuum?

No, it's totally optional: compressing the celery and fennel gives a great texture and translucent appearance. Alternatively cut the vegetables and freeze them the day before, thaw an hour ahead, pat dry and refrigerate; ice crystals rupture the cell walls for a similar effect.
How do you make the pumpernickel croutons?
Heat 1 inch of oil in a very small pot to about 260°F and slowly fry the 1/4-inch cubes until darkened and crispy, about 10 minutes, then drain on paper towels.
What else could I add?
A few pickled grapes would be really good, and toasted or lightly candied walnuts or pecans could replace or supplement the pumpernickel.

summary: Improvised chickpea, spinach and tomato soup: a pound of chickpeas cooked tender (about 40 minutes in a pressure cooker), partly pureed in their cooking liquid for body, then simmered with spinach, tomatoes, lemon, onion and garlic and finished with dukkah; serves 6.
glance: Prep 30 minutes, cook 2 hours (mostly bean boiling time)
1 pound dry chickpeas; reserve 2 cups cooking liquid
olive oil, pepper, parsley and a dusting of dukkah
faq: How do you make the soup thick without cream?

Puree 1 1/2 cups of the cooked beans with 2 cups of their cooking liquid, 2 teaspoons of salt and 2 tablespoons of olive oil, strain it, and add it to the whole chickpeas. It should be fairly thick but not a stew.
Are home-cooked chickpeas better than canned?
The author says they are miles better. Soak overnight and boil until tender, or pressure cook (about 40 minutes at high pressure with a natural release for his pot).
How do I make it Italian instead of North African?
Skip the dukkah and add freshly grated parmesan or pecorino and/or fennel tops or fennel pollen.
Can I use it as a template?
Yes, the author hopes you will use it as a template for your own improvisation. It started as a pure improvisation from an almost empty vegetable drawer.
What did the author serve with it?
A pizza bianca topped with caramelized onions and blue cheese.

summary: Banh xeo, a crispy vegan Vietnamese crepe of rice flour, coconut milk and turmeric filled with mushrooms, tofu, onion and bean sprouts, wrapped in lettuce with fresh herbs and dipped in vegetarian nuoc cham; serves 6 in 45 minutes.
glance: 1 cup rice flour (not sweet rice flour), 1 1/2 cups coconut milk, turmeric, green onions
10-inch non-stick skillet with sloping sides and a lid

summary: Sichuan dry-fried green beans and tofu: tofu browned, then green beans fried in 4 tablespoons of oil until shriveled and blackened in spots (4-10 minutes), drained and tossed with Sichuan preserved vegetable, ginger, garlic and a soy-sesame sauce; 25 minutes.
glance: 2 with rice as a meal, or 4 as part of a larger spread
1/3 cup finely chopped Sichuan preserved vegetable
Vegan; gluten-free with a wheat-free soy sauce
faq: What is in dry-fried green beans?

The yummy brown stuff is Sichuan preserved vegetable, a pickled mustard tuber found canned at a good Asian grocery, along with garlic and ginger. The author was surprised there could be 1/2 cup of garlic in a plate of green beans.
How do I buy Sichuan preserved vegetable?
It's better to buy the large-chunk style and chop it yourself. If you buy it pre-shredded, rinse off some of the salt. The taste is somewhat like kimchi.
How do you dry-fry green beans?

Fry rinsed, dried beans in plenty of hot oil, stirring occasionally, until somewhat shriveled and developing black spots in many places, 4-10 minutes depending on your stove. Then drain, leaving about 1 tablespoon of oil, and toss with the aromatics.
Why dry the green beans?
Rinsed and dried beans avoid spattering. Don't be scared by the quantity of oil or stint on it; most is drained off before the dish is completed.
Why add tofu and mushrooms?
They turn the traditional side dish into a one-dish supper for two, or a hearty part of a larger dinner for four.

summary: Vegetarian japchae, a guest recipe from Alice of Savory Sweet Life: sweet potato starch noodles (dangmyeon) boiled 5 minutes and tossed with soy and sesame oil, then each vegetable and the tofu stir-fried separately for seconds to minutes and combined with sugar, soy and sesame seeds.
glance: 2-3 as a main dish or 4-6 as a side dish
1 bundle dangmyeon, boiled 5 minutes, not rinsed
stir-fry each vegetable individually, from 10 seconds (green onion) to 2 minutes (onion, bell pepper)
Vegetarian and vegan; gluten-free with gluten-free soy sauce
yield: 2-3 as a main dish or 4-6 as a side dish
faq: What is japchae?

A very popular Korean stir-fried noodle dish, also spelled jap chae or chapchae, full of vibrantly colored vegetables stir-fried with glass-looking sweet potato starch noodles (dangmyeon) and seasoned with sesame oil, soy sauce, salt, pepper and a touch of sugar.
Why stir-fry each ingredient separately?
Alice's mother taught her that frying each vegetable individually preserves its flavor and color without cross-blending. The pan also becomes more seasoned as layers of umami build on each other.
Where do I buy dangmyeon?
At any Korean grocery or most Asian markets. Most packages contain 2-3 bundles; this recipe uses one.
How do I cook the noodles?
Boil one bundle for 5 minutes until softened and al dente, drain without rinsing, cut three times with kitchen shears and toss with 2 tablespoons each of soy sauce and sesame oil.
Is it vegan and gluten-free?
It is vegetarian, vegan and gluten-free if you use gluten-free soy sauce; the recipe suggests San-J.
Can I serve it cold?
Yes, japchae is served warm or cold.

summary: Orecchiette with garlic scapes, ricotta and gremolata: 1 pound of scapes sauteed 10 minutes or more in butter and shallot, deglazed with white wine and butter, tossed with dried orecchiette and topped with fresh ricotta and a lemon, parsley, garlic and tarragon gremolata; serves 4.
glance: 1 pound, trimmed and cut in 1 1/2-inch lengths, sauteed 10 minutes or more until mostly tender
lemon zest, garlic, parsley and optional tarragon
1 1/2 cups fresh; the author recommends the Calabro brand
faq: What are garlic scapes?
The firmer central flowering stem of the garlic plant, unlike tender green garlic. When fully cooked they have a texture similar to asparagus and a sweet flavor like slow-roasted garlic.
Where do I find garlic scapes?
Most likely at a farmer's market, though the author has seen them at Asian groceries and Whole Foods.
How do I keep scapes from being woody?
Trim off enough of the hardest part, and cook them fully until tender, which can take 10 minutes or more. If they fight you, add a little water and cover to steam.
What is gremolata?
A mixture of minced lemon zest, parsley and raw garlic that most famously garnishes osso buco. Here a few tarragon leaves add complexity.
What ricotta should I use?
Quality varies widely. If you don't know an excellent local source, the author recommends the national brand Calabro.
What inspired the dish?
A ravioli that Mike Easton served at Il Corvo in Seattle. This version uses good dried orecchiette instead of fresh pasta.

summary: Maple-roasted shiitakes: 1 pound of shiitake caps tossed with about 1/2 cup of real maple syrup, salt and a pinch of smoked paprika and roasted at 400°F, turning, until tender, glazed and wrinkled; served here with cheesy grits and a 5:10 egg.
glance: 4 as part of an entree, or as a breakfast item or side dish
400°F, turning a couple of times, until tender, glazed and wrinkled
about 1/2 cup real maple syrup (Grade A Dark Amber, grade B or bourbon-barrel)
faq: Which maple syrup should I use?

Always real maple. The author used to recommend grade B for more flavor, but Grade A Dark Amber gives intense flavor without underlying bitterness, and bourbon-barrel maple syrup adds a wonderful oaked flavor. Never use artificial maple-flavored syrup.
How do you roast the mushrooms?
Toss the stemmed caps with syrup, salt and smoked paprika, spread in a single layer on a lined baking sheet and roast at 400°F, turning a couple of times, until tender, glazed and wrinkled.
What is a 5:10 egg?

David Chang's egg: add refrigerator-cold eggs to a simmering pot, set a timer for exactly 5 minutes 10 seconds, then transfer to an ice bath and peel. The result has a fully set white and a liquid but viscous yolk. You can rewarm in water below 140°F (60°C) for a minute.
How do I get eggs that peel cleanly?
Age matters. As eggs get a little older, the air pocket gets bigger and helps them separate from the shell, so buy eggs for peeling further in advance.
What did the author serve them with?
Cheesy grits and a 5:10 egg, with radishes, parsley salt and rosemary flowers. At a popup dinner he used king oyster mushrooms the same way.

summary: Arancini di riso: arborio risotto cooled, stirred with an egg, formed into golf-ball-sized balls around cubes of scamorza, breaded in fresh breadcrumbs and deep-fried at about 360°F; the balls can be formed a day ahead; makes about 12.
glance: 1 1/4 cups arborio (must be a risotto rice) with 4 cups clear vegetable broth
oil at about 360°F, in small batches, until deep brown
form the balls and refrigerate, well wrapped, for a day
Vegetarian; not vegan; gluten-free with gluten-free breadcrumbs and broth

summary: Roasted potato and asparagus tacos in a Mexico City street-taco style: cumin-roasted Yukon gold potatoes and asparagus with kohlrabi slaw, avocado, feta or cotija and lemon crema in two steamed corn tortillas; makes 8 tacos.
glance: 8 tacos, serves 4 with rice and beans
potatoes at 375°F until golden and crispy; asparagus about 10 minutes
kohlrabi (or jicama), onion and orange-muscat champagne vinegar
Vegetarian and gluten-free; not vegan unless you omit the dairy
yield: 8 tacos, serves 4 with rice and beans
faq: What is a Mexico City-style taco?
Soft tacos with just a fistful of delicious ingredients in two soft, steamed corn tortillas, perfect to pick up in one hand and never put back down, rather than overstuffed tacos that need a fork.
What corn tortillas should I use?
In order of preference: homemade, from a local tortilleria, or a national Mexican brand. The author says not to buy the ones at Whole Foods: the texture is wrong and they get crumbly when heated.
Can I use something other than kohlrabi?
Yes. Kohlrabi was the nicest-looking crispy vegetable at the market, but jicama works just as well. Julienne it on a mandoline or grate it.
What vinegar goes in the slaw?
The author used Trader Joe's Orange Muscat Champagne vinegar. You can combine 1/4 cup champagne vinegar and 1/4 cup fresh orange juice.
How do I keep the tacos hot?

Have hot plates and all ingredients prepared and organized in advance. Warm the plates in a 175°F oven with the potatoes and asparagus, and steam the tortillas wrapped in a moist towel in the microwave, checking after 1 minute.
Is cotija better than feta?
The author says the feta should obviously have been cotija, but feta was what he had on hand.
